problem.consequence: Simply allowing multiple registries without an explicit per-fact write authority can create duplicate cardinality-one Current facts for the same Subject + fact_key across registry versions.

designPrinciples: Registry version existence/effectiveness and Registry write authority are separate concepts.
Exactly one registry version may be write-authoritative for a given fact_key at a time.
Existing v1 fact keys remain write-authoritative on v1 until an explicit fact-key migration is completed.
The new broad_spectrum fact_key may be write-authoritative on a future v2 without migrating unrelated v1 fact keys.
Current Facts and definitions remain immutable.
Recommendation consumers do not automatically follow registry publication.
Existing fact_key migration requires a separate drain/migration protocol; registry publication alone never migrates Facts.

proposedPolicyTable.name: product_fact_registry_fact_write_policy_v1
proposedPolicyTable.purpose: Explicit per-registry/per-fact controlled-write authority, independent from global latest registry selection.
proposedPolicyTable.invariant: At most one registry_version can have new_lineage_allowed=true for the same fact_key at a time.

proposedAdmissibilityHelper.name: product_fact_controlled_registry_write_admissibility_v2
rules: Registry version must exist and the requested fact definition must exist and be non-deprecated.
For lineage_kind=new, new_lineage_allowed must be true.
For lineage_kind=existing, existing_lineage_allowed must be true.
Blocked or expired policy fails closed.
A newer registry_version alone never invalidates a pinned existing lineage.

writePathChanges.replacement: new assignment -> require new lineage authority; existing open assignment transition -> require existing lineage authority

writePathChanges.currentGate: confirmation payload registry participates in latest-registry prestate
writePathChanges.replacement: require existing-lineage authority for the assignment registry/fact_key; include write-policy digest in prestate

writePathChanges.currentGate: candidate registry must equal global latest registry
writePathChanges.replacement: candidate research lineage must have existing-lineage authority for its pinned registry/fact_key

writePathChanges.currentGate: legacy revalidation coupled to latest registry
writePathChanges.replacement: revalidation transition remains pinned to its existing registry and requires existing-lineage authority

v1.policy: existing 20 fact keys remain active for both new and existing lineage until each fact_key is explicitly migrated

futureV2.definitionModel: full immutable snapshot may include existing definitions plus broad_spectrum

requiredBeforeSwitch: Block creation of new lineage on old registry for the target fact_key.
Drain or explicitly disposition all old-registry active lineages for that fact_key.
Verify no cross-version cardinality-one Current ambiguity exists.
Define explicit Current replacement/supersession semantics across registry versions.
Update affected consumers if they require single-registry lineage.
Only then block old existing-lineage writes and enable new-registry writes for that fact_key.
sameFactKeyMigrationProtocol.reason: broad_spectrum is a new fact_key, so it does not collide with existing v1 fact keys.

cardinalityBoundary.risk: The current guard does not prevent the same cardinality-one fact_key from existing as Current in both v1 and v2.
mitigation: Enforce one write-authoritative registry per fact_key in the write-policy layer.
Do not enable existing fact keys on v2 until the explicit migration protocol is implemented.
Before future same-key migration, add or prove a cross-registry Current replacement guard.

recommendationBoundary.reason: The current reader requires a single registry_version across the three consumed protection facts.

implementationOrder: Add per-fact registry write-policy storage and fail-closed admin management boundary.
Seed current v1 fact-key write authority without changing any Fact or consumer.
Replace four global-latest write gates with lineage-aware admissibility checks.
Bind write-policy state into confirmation prestate digest so policy changes invalidate stale confirmation.
Add regression tests proving v1 active lineage remains completable after a second registry exists.
Add tests proving an unauthorized fact_key/registry pair fails closed.
Add tests proving same fact_key cannot become write-authoritative in two registries simultaneously.
Keep Recommendation sunscreen authority reader/projection unchanged.
Only after all above passes may a future Registry version containing broad_spectrum be published and separately granted write authority.
nonGoals: No Registry v2 publish in R3C.
No Production schema migration in R3C.
No broad_spectrum Product Fact write in R3C.
No Recommendation reader or ranking change.
